title: Seasonal surveillance of chikungunya virus disease in the EU/EEA – 2026 – Weekly

analysis.time: Since the beginning of 2026 and as at 11 November 2026 (N1, N2, N16, N17, N18).
analysis.location_and_population: France (213 cases), Italy (1 case), Switzerland (4 cases in Ticino, not included in ECDC data) (N1, N2, N10, N11, N12).
analysis.event: Seasonal surveillance report on chikungunya virus disease in the EU/EEA, noting locally acquired cases in France and Italy, and first cases in Switzerland (N1, N2, N10, N11).
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: 213 cases in France, 1 case in Italy, and 4 cases in Switzerland (not included in ECDC data). 31 clusters, with 14 active clusters (N1, N2, N4, N6, N7, N8, N10, N11, N12).
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: ECDC continues to monitor the situation and publish weekly reports until November 2026. The newly identified cluster in Switzerland is considered closed (N13, N15, N5, N9).

analysis.brief_en: The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) has released a weekly seasonal surveillance report on chikungunya virus disease in the EU/EEA as of 13 November 2026. The report indicates that two countries in Europe have reported locally acquired cases: France with 213 cases and Italy with one case. Since the last update, France has added six new cases, while Italy has not reported any new cases. The cases are distributed across 31 clusters, with 14 currently active, including the largest in Prayssac (38 cases) and Cavalaire-sur-Mer (34 cases). Notably, Switzerland has reported four locally acquired cases in Ticino, marking the first such cases in the country. However, these are not included in ECDC data as Switzerland does not report to the agency. The newly identified cluster in Ticino is already closed. ECDC will continue monitoring the situation and publish weekly reports until November 2026.
analysis.summary_en: The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) has released a weekly seasonal surveillance report on chikungunya virus disease in the EU/EEA as of 13 November 2026. The report indicates that two countries in Europe have reported locally acquired cases: France with 213 cases and Italy with one case. Since the last update, France has added six new cases, while Italy has not reported any new cases. The cases are distributed across 31 clusters, with 14 currently active, including the largest in Prayssac (38 cases) and Cavalaire-sur-Mer (34 cases). Notably, Switzerland has reported four locally acquired cases in Ticino, marking the first such cases in the country. However, these are not included in ECDC data as Switzerland does not report to the agency. The newly identified cluster in Ticino is already closed. ECDC will continue monitoring the situation and publish weekly reports until November 2026.

The report highlights the rising global challenge of mosquito-borne diseases, including chikungunya, dengue, and Zika virus, which are transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes. The market size is expected to increase from $0.65 billion in 2025 to $0.71 billion in 2026, reflecting a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 9.4%. By 2030, the CAGR is projected to be 9.1%. The report notes that the Asia-Pacific region is expected to experience the fastest growth during the forecast period, while North America held the largest share in 2025. This forecast is based on industry expansion and public health trends, not confirmed outbreaks or cases. title: NCDC confirms dengue in two states, chikungunya in Sokoto - The Guardian Nigeria News

analysis.time: The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) confirmed dengue in two states and chikungunya in Sokoto on 11 November 2026. The index patient in the country’s Ebola outbreak remains positive and hospitalised in Switzerland, with 62 contacts being monitored. The development comes as Nigeria approaches the dry season, a period associated with increased risk of cerebrospinal meningitis and seasonal transmission of Lassa fever. The DG gave the update on Ebola through the agency’s Director of Public Health, Dr Odianosan Ehiakhamen, during a webinar on 11 November 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The NCDC confirmed dengue in Sokoto and Zamfara states, and chikungunya in Sokoto. The NCDC official acknowledged delays in identifying the infection, noting that the patient had initially been treated for malaria and other febrile illnesses.

analysis.brief_en: The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) confirmed dengue fever in Sokoto and Zamfara states, and chikungunya in Sokoto on 11 November 2026. The index patient in the country’s Ebola outbreak remains positive and hospitalised in Switzerland, with 62 contacts being monitored. The NCDC has deployed National Rapid Response Teams, including entomologists, to support affected states with case finding, laboratory investigations, and mosquito control. The DG gave the update on Ebola through the agency’s Director of Public Health, Dr Odianosan Ehiakhamen, during a webinar. The NCDC official acknowledged delays in identifying the infection, noting that the patient had initially been treated for malaria and other febrile illnesses. The NCDC chief warned that dengue and chikungunya could present with symptoms such as fever, headache, body pains, and joint pains, urging Nigerians to seek medical assessment rather than automatically treating every fever as malaria. The development comes as Nigeria approaches the dry season, a period associated with increased risk of cerebrospinal meningitis and seasonal transmission of Lassa fever, prompting calls for strengthened disease surveillance, early detection, and preparedness.

title: Dengue Up 58% in Costa Rica as Chikungunya Passes 1,000 Cases - The Tico Times

analysis.time: The article was published on November 11, 2026. Dengue cases increased by 58% in 2026 compared to the same period last year. Chikungunya reached 1,049 cases by the 42nd epidemiological week of the year, in mid-October.
analysis.location_and_population: The outbreak is primarily in Guanacaste, with the Chorotega health region accounting for 57% of the national total. Alajuela province has the most dengue cases at 2,791, followed by Puntarenas with 981 and San José with 880. Chikungunya cases are also reported in other regions such as La Cruz, Carrillo, and Santa Cruz.
analysis.event: Dengue cases in Costa Rica rose by 58% in 2026, and chikungunya, which had been absent for nearly a decade, surpassed 1,000 cases. The Ministry of Health reported 6,594 dengue cases, with 105 classified as dengue with warning signs. Chikungunya cases include 916 confirmed by lab tests and 133 probable cases still under study.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Dengue cases reached 6,594 in 2026, with 105 classified as severe. Chikungunya cases totaled 1,049, with 916 confirmed and 133 probable. The Ministry of Health and the Costa Rican Social Security System (CCSS) reported these figures. The rise in cases was flagged by the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention as higher-than-expected dengue risk.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The Ministry of Health and CCSS are monitoring the outbreak. Public health measures include using repellent, wearing long sleeves, and eliminating water sources for mosquito breeding. The article mentions that local transmission was first confirmed in July in Guanacaste and Alajuela. The dry season has begun, but water stored in tanks and buckets can still breed mosquitoes.

analysis.brief_en: In November 2026, Costa Rica reported a significant rise in dengue cases, up 58% compared to the same period in 2025, with 6,594 confirmed cases. Chikungunya, which had been absent for nearly a decade, surpassed 1,000 cases by mid-October, with 916 confirmed and 133 probable cases. The outbreak is concentrated in Guanacaste, where the Chorotega health region accounts for 57% of the national total. Alajuela province has the highest number of dengue cases at 2,791, followed by Puntarenas and San José. The Ministry of Health and the Costa Rican Social Security System (CCSS) are tracking the spread, and the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention noted higher-than-expected dengue risk. Public health measures include using repellent, wearing long sleeves, and eliminating water sources for mosquito breeding. The dry season has begun, but stored water can still breed mosquitoes, so containers should be kept covered. The outbreak is a concern due to the potential for severe cases and the need for continued vigilance.
